national_indicator_definition: This indicator measures total antibiotic consumption in human medicine in both the community and hospital sectors. Consumption is expressed as the number of defined daily doses (DDD) per 1,000 inhabitants per day (DID). At the European Union level, the indicator covers antibacterials for systemic use belonging to ATC group J01.
national_rationale: The data source is the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), through the European Surveillance of Antimicrobial Consumption Network (ESAC-Net). Data are collected annually and cover antibiotic consumption in both the community and hospital sectors. Consumption is expressed in defined daily doses (DDD) per 1,000 inhabitants per day (DID), in accordance with the World Health Organization's ATC/DDD methodology. The European Union aggregate represents a population-weighted mean, with imputation and adjustment procedures applied where necessary to address missing data.
national_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers antibacterials for systemic use belonging to ATC group J01, used in human medicine in both the community and hospital sectors. Expressing consumption in DDD per 1,000 inhabitants per day enables monitoring of changes over time and comparison between countries applying harmonised data collection and processing methodologies. Data are available annually.
national_long_objective: Reducing unnecessary and inappropriate antibiotic use is an important element of efforts to combat antimicrobial resistance in the European Union. The 2023 Council Recommendation on stepping up EU actions to combat antimicrobial resistance sets a target of reducing total antibiotic consumption in human medicine by 20% by 2030, compared with 2019. This target applies to the population-weighted consumption at the European Union level.
